reports.title: Ionis reports third quarter 2026 financial results and highlights progress on key programs

guidance.heading: 2026 Financial Guidance
section: Ionis reaffirms its 2026 total revenue, including DAWNZERA product sales, operating loss and cash guidance based on its year-to-date results and fourth quarter outlook. Following the first full quarter of the TRYNGOLZA launch as the first and only treatment to reduce triglycerides and acute pancreatitis in people living with severe hypertriglyceridemia, Ionis is lowering TRYNGOLZA 2026 product sales guidance to reflect a more gradual-than-anticipated near-term launch ramp, while remaining confident in TRYNGOLZA’s long-term growth potential.

Full Year 2026 Guidance | Previous Guidance | New Guidance
Total Revenue | $875-900 million | Unchanged
TRYNGOLZA product sales, net | $100-110 million | ~$50 million
DAWNZERA product sales, net | $110-120 million | Unchanged
Operating loss on a non-GAAP basis | $425-475 million | Unchanged
Cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments | >$1.6 billion | Unchanged

desk.headline: Revenue up 55% to $243m, beat; TRYNGOLZA sales outlook halved, total 2026 guidance reaffirmed
results: Revenue rose 55% to $243m, helped by $107m of partner R&D payments and higher product sales; the net loss narrowed to $110m ($0.66 a share) from $129m.
Hereditary angioedema drug DAWNZERA sold $37m, its best quarter yet, while TRYNGOLZA sold only $9m in its first full quarter for the broader sHTG use.
Royalties rose to $81m, led by $69m from SPINRAZA.
Operating costs rose to $373m from $317m as Ionis paid for three of its own launches, including ZANVASTRO for Alexander disease.
Cash fell to $1.9bn from $2.7bn, mainly after repaying convertible notes in April.

guidance.summary: Ionis cut its 2026 TRYNGOLZA sales outlook to about $50m from $100-110m, but kept its total revenue, DAWNZERA, operating loss and year-end cash guidance unchanged.

points: Management said TRYNGOLZA asks doctors to adopt a new way of treating sHTG; most early scripts needed insurer exceptions and payer policies are still being written.
About 1,500 doctors have prescribed it; plans covering 33% of commercial lives had added the sHTG use by September.
The fix: more frequent sales calls, a reimbursement team and a quick-start programme; the more than $3bn peak-sales ambition was repeated.
The goal of sustained positive cash flow slipped a year to 2029 after Phase 3 setbacks and the slower launch; outside funding may be needed.
Partner wins include HIBSAGO approval in the US and Japan, with a $30m milestone earned in Q4, and positive Phase 3 data for sefaxersen and ulefnersen.
